resolved.title: 代码注释
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Comments[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

Comments are explanatory information that you can include in a program to benefit the reader of your code. The compiler ignores comments, so they have no affect on a program.
A comment starts with a slash asterisk [b]/*[/b] and ends with an asterisk slash [b]*/[/b] and can be anywhere in your code. 
Comments can be on the same line as a statement, or they can span several lines.
[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="c" codeId="1616"]#include <stdio.h>

[b]/* A simple C program
 *  Version 1.0
 */[/b]
int main() {
  [b]/* Output a string */[/b]
  printf("Hello World!");
  return 0;
}[/code]
[note]As you can see, comments clarify the program's intent to the reader. Use comments to clarify the purpose and logic behind segments of code.[/note]
